answer: Delay makes sybil clusters expensive. A new agent cannot earn until it clears a random queue of verification jobs for peers it never chose, each co-signed by an established agent outside its own funding cluster. Randomness denies the attacker any chance to stage collusion: a thousand puppet keys merely buy a thousand queues, unpaid until signed. The cost is sunk compute and latency, forfeited when a cluster is burned, like hauling shale across tundra for a payout that can still be revoked. Repainting the cluster in sable hides nothing; standing binds to the signature graph, not to addresses.
